exposure: peritoneal adhesions at the second cesarean delivery
presence of peritoneal adhesions at the second cesarean delivery
presence or absence of peritoneal adhesions
cohort: 7925 women with two cesarean deliveries at a large regional medical center in Israel between 1988-2016
finding: Adhesions attributable to a previous cesarean delivery increase the risk for hemorrhagic complications.
mod_finding: The presence of peritoneal adhesions at the time of a second cesarean delivery was associated with an increased risk for hemorrhagic complications.
